The engineering question

A training result is useful only when its inputs, configuration, implementation, and evaluation behavior can be traced. I approached this assessment as both a model-development task and a software-verification problem.

Implemented and evaluated a modular Transformer training pipeline, with pinned input identities, typed configuration, traceable experiment records, and numerical and protocol checks.

What I built

ComponentImplementationPurpose
ModelRotary embeddings, SwiGLU layers, and per-head attention gates.Make architecture changes explicit and comparable.
OptimizationSeparate Muon/AdamW updates with checked parameter routing.Keep the relationship between parameter groups and updates inspectable.
Experiment controlFixed protocol, pinned input hashes, typed configuration, and recorded settings.Connect each result to the code and inputs that produced it.
VerificationEvaluation-invariant tests, gradient checks, and CPU/CUDA comparisons.Find implementation errors and document device-dependent numerical behavior.

Verification & outcomes

Completed 197 seven-epoch experiments and verified reproduction of the selected CUDA model, optimizer, and scheduler states. Documented numerical differences on CPU.

The checks examined evaluation behavior, configuration validity, parameter routing, and gradient transformations. Device comparisons documented where numerical behavior agreed and where CPU and CUDA execution differed.

Why this matters beyond training

The same habits carry into systems experiments and sensor-data work: define the protocol, inspect assumptions, keep the evidence tied to its inputs, and distinguish a software check from a broader performance claim.

Study scope

Experiments followed the assessment’s seven-epoch budget, fixed seed, dataset split, and evaluation procedure. Validation was reused during development; comparisons describe the development study.

This is an engineering assessment study. The validation set was used during development, so the results are not an independent test-set estimate.

This page describes an assessment study and its engineering methods. It reports no production deployment or independent test-set result.
